cfo_chris: Thanks everyone for joining the finance segment of today's all-hands. Quick live Q&A on burn, spend controls, and procurement — ask away.

maya_eng: Appreciate it Chris. Quick one — what runway are we projecting after the Series C spend?

cfo_chris: We still have ~20 months at current burn. That number assumes Dedicated capacity growth as forecasted and some new enterprise deals. We plan to tighten discretionary spend in Q2. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

kevin_procurement: For procurement folks — any immediate changes to POs or approvals we should expect?

cfo_chris: Approval thresholds unchanged for committed contract items. For ad-hoc software/hardware purchases > $15k we'll require a Finance + Eng manager signoff and a short procurement justification.

sofia_peopleops: Are we pausing hiring across the board or just non-critical roles?
cfo_chris: No blanket freeze. Hiring will be prioritized: critical customer-facing and product/infra roles first. All reqs need a hiring justification form routed to Finance -> Hiring Committee.

alexa_engmgr: Can you clarify "discretionary spend"? Does that include conference budgets and training credits?
cfo_chris: Yes — conferences, vendor swag, and generic training are in scope. We'll allow exceptions for customer-facing activities with a clear ROI case.

devin_product: Any changes to capital vs operating classification for our Dedicated hardware? Some teams prefer capex to manage depreciation for budget lines.
cfo_chris: We're evaluating a hybrid approach. Short-term Dedicated bursts will be OPEX; larger multi-year reserved capacity can be capitalized if contract terms meet capex criteria. Finance will publish guidance next week.

matt_ops: For urgent infra replacement (failed GPU nodes), who signs off for emergency spend?
kevin_procurement: Ops can use the emergency procurement path: email procurement + on-call finance and get verbal approval. Please tag #eng-oncall and cc procurement. We'll follow-up with retro docs.

maya_eng: Will there be stricter controls on third-party ML compute costs (e.g., spot instances, burst TPU usage)?
cfo_chris: Yes. Starting next billing cycle, teams using cloud burst must register the workload and provide expected spend cap. Finance will enforce soft limits and alert owners when 80% of cap is reached.

finance_bot: [Automated] New spend guardrails template created: /docs/finance/spend-guardrails-v1.pdf :page_with_curl:

kevin_procurement: Sharing simplified procurement request template (please use this for anything > $5k):

```
Procurement Request:
- Requester: <name>
- Team: <team>
- Item/Service: <description>
- Estimated cost: <$amount>
- Business justification: <1-2 sentences>
- Impact if denied: <short>
- Approval chain: <mgr>, procurement, finance
```

alexa_engmgr: Nice. Can procurement enforce contract templates for vendor security (SOC2)? We're seeing a lot of non-standard terms from small vendors.

kevin_procurement: Yes — anything processing customer data must include our security addendum. Procurement will flag non-compliant contracts and pause onboarding until legal/security review completes.

sofia_peopleops: How will spend controls affect team training stipends that are already in onboarding flows?
cfo_chris: We want to protect onboarding essentials. Training stipends under $500 per head for role-specific onboarding remain allowed; discretionary learning budgets will be paused for Q2 pending evaluation.

devin_product: Will this change affect marketing campaigns that are in-flight? We have several paid pilots running.
cfo_chris: Active SLAs and ongoing pilots will be honored. New campaigns will need an expected ROI estimate and an owner. Marketing should tag these requests as "pilot" in the procurement template.

maya_eng: If teams hit an unexpected spend spike, is there a fast appeal path?
cfo_chris: Yes — submit an urgent spend review with the procurement template + root cause. We'll triage within 48 hours. If it's customer-impacting ops, escalate to on-call finance.

matt_ops: Any change to vendor onboarding SLA? We often need faster onboarding for infra suppliers.

kevin_procurement: We're aiming for a 5-business-day SLA for standard vendors; critical infra vendors can be expedited with manager + procurement signoff.

alexa_engmgr: Request: Can Finance publish a simple dashboard showing month-to-date committed spend per team? Helps managers track.
cfo_chris: Yes, we'll prioritize a per-team MTD committed spend view in Console. ETA: 2 weeks.

devin_product: Will there be any immediate changes to our customer credits policy? Some sales deals are tied to usage credits.
cfo_chris: Customer credits tied to signed deals remain. Finance will review any ad-hoc credits > $50k.

matt_ops: Action item: I'll compile a short list of critical infra vendors to label "expedited" and send to procurement.

kevin_procurement: Sounds good. Please include expected spend cadence.

sofia_peopleops: Follow-up for HR: we'll update the onboarding docs to reflect training stipend exception.

cfo_chris: Thanks all — follow-up items: 1) Finance to publish capex/opex guidance (next week), 2) Procurement template link and 5-day SLA, 3) MTD committed spend view in Console (2 weeks). I'll post notes and links in #announcements. :spiral_notepad:

finance_bot: [Automated] Follow-up doc created: /internal/finance/q2-spend-control-actions.md

maya_eng: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone.

alexa_engmgr: Appreciate the clarity.

kevin_procurement: Will send the template and a short how-to later today.

cfo_chris: If anyone needs 1:1 clarification, my calendar is open for the next few days.

matt_ops: Thanks Chris — good session. :eyes:
